This case was deliberately red until 2026-08-17 and is now fixed at the cause: getCompletionCategoryForSymbol was keyed by bare simple NAME and resolved a collision by first match, filing FLine.moveTo under Math (from stdlib/Functions.kt) and close/rot/scale/copy under Solvers/Patterns/Synthesis/Audio, in foreign SECTIONS that no ranking term can cross. cases.label: List bare dot
cases.note: OFF-SCREEN since 2026-10-16, and accepted. CATEGORY_WEIGHT now carries the server vocabulary (variant R2 of dev_docs/completion_rank_at_scale.md: server categories 12, Kotlin 8, External 4), which over the 578-caret corpus raises bare contested recall by 0.051 and recall on receivers this tree cannot annotate by 0.120, with owned recall unchanged. The same study measured the cost on named cases: answers that stay visible arrive later, List members among them. `filter` sat at 77 of 80, at the cutoff, and the categorised rows that now outrank it push it past 80. It is a kotlin.collections extension on a foreign receiver, which no @CommonMembers prior can reach. Type `l.fil` to reach it (see `String two chars`). Before this change: 77 of 80 visible after the package cutover. Concrete receiver conformance excludes List<Vec3> and other incompatible extensions from List<Int>; generic Iterable<T> extensions remain. The real K2 recording contains 278 candidates. This ratchet holds the measured rank at 77. `filter` is a kotlin.collections extension, not a List member, and this tree cannot attach a prior to the foreign receiver. It moved from 71 to 78 when package-scoped category lookup stopped borrowing the first categorised file in filesystem order: the seven places were classification noise, not a ranking signal, and the same fix makes all 6,679 corpus rows deterministic under a shuffled source walk. Kotlin is unweighted in CATEGORY_WEIGHT, so `filter` remains near the alphabetical cutoff. To reach a known member, type `l.fil`; see `String two chars` for the prefixed shape.

cases.label: Math qualifier
cases.note: OFF-SCREEN, and accepted. All 109 java.lang.Math rows now classify as External -- correctly and UNIFORMLY -- so they tie on CATEGORY_WEIGHT and the list collapses to the server's alphabetical order: E, IEEEremainder, PI, TAU, abs, abs... `toRadians` is past row 80 of 110. Its old rank of 52 was not a ranking decision, it was misclassification noise. java.lang.Math cannot carry a @CommonMembers prior, so a bare `Math.` has no prior and no weight and alphabetical is the honest answer -- the same argument that says nobody reaches moveTo by scanning 249 rows. Since 2026-10-16 External carries a weight (4), but uniformly, so the order inside the bucket is still alphabetical.
